WTI.label: WTI Oct
WTI.source: October 2026 contract, +$2.96, Reuters energy desk with an explicit 0903 GMT dateline and a named reporter. The contract has NOT rolled - Investing.com confirms Oct 26, settlement 09/22, last rollover 08/20 - and five independent feeds all price off the same $83.40 Friday settle, which is the proof the gap is real rather than a vendor artefact. It gapped to an $84.60 open on the Sunday 6 p.m. ET reopen, has ground higher through Asia and Europe, printed a high of $86.78, and was STILL FIRMING into 6 a.m.: MarketWatch's 5:57 a.m. strip is the highest read at $86.59, +3.82%. THE DRIVER IS A HOPE TRADE UNWINDING, NOT JUST A RISK PREMIUM, and that is why 3.5% is not an overreaction. Crude fell more than 4% LAST week - its first weekly decline in three - because Iran and Oman were reported to be negotiating a reopening of the strait. Those talks collapsed, then US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island after observing IRGC units preparing to fire rockets carrying SEA MINES into the strait. The market is unwinding a reopening it had already paid for. The curve confirms it is disruption pricing rather than a structural re-rating: Oct +2.02, Nov +1.89, Dec +1.84 - the front moved most. Physical flow is the number that matters: Hormuz crude exports averaged 3.8m bpd over the past week against 9.8m bpd during the 25-day ceasefire, Iranian exports are at ZERO, and visible transits fell to five a day. UKMTO Warning 122-26 reports a crude tanker struck by a projectile 12nm north of Khasab, the THIRD strait attack in a week. Two cautions, both material. Ole Hansen at Saxo notes the reaction is amplified by thin volumes with London closed. And part of this rally may be priced on an AI-GENERATED VIDEO the President posted claiming Kharg Island was destroyed - no military confirmation, an Iranian official called it laughable. If that is in the price, it is reversal risk. Rejected sources: CNBC @CL.1 at 83.44 is Friday's data, oilprice.com at 82.12 is roughly Aug 27 vintage and points the WRONG way, Barchart self-labels Aug 27
